feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 4 (0.8 kg, 0.16 m body, 0.10 m track, y = 0.03 m) gave oval oscillation 0.181, line loss 0 on the oval and s-bend, and max_error 0.0614 m. Iteration 1 (0.12 m track, same mass and body) gave oscillation 0.173, so restoring inertia brought oscillation down and track width did not. Max_error has stayed at 0.061 to 0.064 m through every iteration, so the reaction point is the lever to test. I held the iteration 4 controller fixed (kp 2.8, kd 0.35, base_speed 1.4), so the race isolates the row move. If max_error falls below 0.06 m with oscillation at or below 0.2, keep y = 0.02 m and test wheel_radius 0.035 m only if oval progress stays below 0.35. If oscillation rises above 0.2 while max_error does not move, the controller is reacting too late to the row, so the next Integrator move is kd up toward 0.4, and the geometry should stay as it is. If line_loss rises on the slalom (it was 0.25 at y = 0.03 m, iteration 3), the row is too close for the sharper bends, so try sensor_size 0.012 at the same positions.
requested_changes: If oval progress stays below 0.35 with max_error near 0.061 m (iteration 4 gave progress 0.34): try wheel_radius 0.035 m with the same mass 0.8 kg and body, since progress has tracked speed and the wheel radius is the speed lever.

If line_loss_events rise above about 0.25 on the slalom after the row moves to y = 0.02 m (iteration 3 at y = 0.03 m and 0.06 m-wide sensor span gave 0.25): try sensor_size 0.012 at the same x and y positions to narrow the footprint near the outer sensors.

If max_error stays at 0.061 to 0.064 m across the y = 0.02 m test and oscillation is low: stop geometry changes for max_error, because iterations 0 to 4 showed no geometry response, and try a lower-inertia mass of 0.7 kg with wheel_radius 0.035 m for speed instead.
